title: Scholarship Application
text: You are volunteering at your school and helping students with their questions. A student asks you how to apply for a scholarship, but you don't know the specific application process. What would you say to the student?
facts: A student asks a school volunteer how to apply for a scholarship.
Be honest about not knowing the procedure and help the student find official guidance.
sample: I’m not sure of the exact application process, but I can help you find out. Let’s check the school scholarship page together, or I can show you where the student services office is so you can ask about eligibility, forms and deadlines.

title: Damaged Student ID
text: Your student ID card is damaged, and you can no longer use it to enter the campus building. You need to ask the campus administrator for help and request a replacement card. What would you say?
facts: The damaged student ID no longer opens the campus building.
Ask the campus administrator for a replacement and instructions for getting access meanwhile.
sample: Hello, my student ID card has been damaged and it no longer lets me into the campus building. Could you tell me how to get a replacement? I have the damaged card with me. Is there a temporary way I can access the building while the new card is being issued?

title: Academic Conference
text: Your tutor has invited you to attend an academic conference. You are interested but unsure how you should prepare and how attending the conference could benefit your academic development. What would you say to your tutor?
facts: The tutor invited the student to an academic conference.
Show interest and ask how to prepare and how the conference might support academic development.
sample: Thank you for inviting me to the conference. I’d like to go. Is there anything I should read beforehand or any sessions you think I should attend? I’d also appreciate your advice on how I could use the conference to develop my research interests.

title: Dormitory Noise
text: You live in a college dormitory, and your upstairs neighbors frequently make a lot of noise. You want to complain about the situation to the dormitory manager. What would you say to the manager?
facts: Frequent noise from upstairs affects the resident.
Report the issue politely to the dormitory manager and ask them to help resolve it.
sample: Hello, could I ask for your help with a noise issue? The residents in the room above mine have been quite loud on several occasions. It’s been difficult to relax in my room. Could you speak with them or let me know how to raise the issue formally?

title: Dietary Requirements
text: You are in charge of a student society and are organizing a welcome dinner for new members. You need to find out whether any participants have dietary restrictions or need to avoid certain foods. What would you say to the participants?
facts: A student society is planning a welcome dinner for new members.
Ask participants about food restrictions and allergies before ordering.
sample: Hi everyone, we’re organising a welcome dinner for our new members. Could you please let me know if you have any food allergies, dietary restrictions or ingredients you need to avoid? You can message me privately so we can plan suitable options before we confirm the menu.

title: Sports Club Membership
text: You want to persuade your friend to join a sports club because you think it would be beneficial for him. However, you also want to remind him to consider the cost involved. What would you say to your friend?
facts: Joining a sports club could benefit a friend.
Encourage the friend to consider joining while checking whether the costs are affordable.
sample: I think you’d enjoy joining a sports club. You could get regular exercise and meet people who like the same sport. Before signing up, though, check the membership fees and whether you’ll need to buy equipment. A trial session might help you decide whether it’s worth the cost.

title: Business Dinner
text: You are having dinner with a business partner. One of your neighbors runs a company that could be suitable for collaboration. You would like to invite your neighbor to join you for dinner and discuss potential business opportunities. What would you say to your neighbor?
facts: The neighbor’s company might be a good fit for collaboration with a business partner.
Invite the neighbor to join dinner and explore shared business opportunities.
sample: Hi, I’m having dinner with a business partner and I thought there could be a good opportunity for us to work with your company. Would you like to join us? It would be a chance to meet each other and discuss whether there’s a project we could collaborate on.

title: Work-Study Balance
text: Your friend is working part-time to help pay for her course fees. Because she performs exceptionally well at work, her manager has offered her a full-time position with a high salary and attractive benefits. However, accepting the offer may interfere with her studies. What advice would you give her?
facts: A friend has a lucrative full-time job offer but needs time for her studies.
Acknowledge the benefits and advise her to consider study commitments and negotiate flexibility.
sample: The salary and benefits sound tempting, especially with your course fees. Before accepting, check how the hours would fit around lectures and assignments. Could you ask your manager whether they’d consider flexible hours or let you stay part-time until you finish your course? I’d make sure you can still keep up with your studies before deciding.

title: Studying in Cafe
text: You're studying in a coffee shop, but it's about to close. Since you need to keep studying late into the evening, you ask one of the staff if there are any other coffee shops nearby that are still open. What would you say?
facts: A coffee shop is closing and the student needs to continue studying.
Ask a staff member about another nearby café that stays open late.
sample: Excuse me, I see you’re about to close. I still have some studying to do this evening. Do you know of another café nearby where I could sit and work for a while? If you know how late it stays open, that would be really helpful.

title: Interview and Lecture
text: You have a job interview scheduled with a local store, but you have just realised that it clashes with one of your lectures. You need to contact the manager and request a different interview time. What would you say?
facts: A store job interview clashes with a lecture.
Contact the store manager, show continued interest and request a different time.
sample: Hello, I’m calling about my interview at your store. I’ve just realised the appointment clashes with a lecture. I’m still very interested in the job. Would it be possible to move the interview to another time? I can come in after class or at another time that suits you.

title: Sport and Class
text: You often arrive late for class because you take part in your favorite sport every Thursday afternoon. How would you explain this to your teacher?
facts: Playing a sport on Thursday afternoons has repeatedly made the student late.
Explain the conflict to the teacher, acknowledge responsibility and offer to prevent it recurring.
sample: I wanted to explain why I’ve been arriving late on Thursdays. I play a sport that afternoon and I haven’t been leaving enough time to get to class. I’m sorry for the disruption. I’ll speak with my coach about leaving earlier so I can be on time.

title: Tired Friend
text: Your friend says she has been feeling very tired recently. You know she often stays up late. What would you say?
facts: A friend has been feeling tired and often stays up late.
Show concern and gently suggest a change in sleep routine.
sample: You’ve mentioned feeling tired a lot lately, and I know you’ve been staying up quite late. Do you think going to bed a bit earlier for a few nights might help? Is anything making it difficult for you to get enough sleep?

title: Assignment Comment
text: Your tutor has commented on your assignment, "Write more academically." You want to understand what they mean. What would you say?
facts: The tutor wrote “Write more academically” on an assignment.
Ask what the comment means and request a concrete example of how to improve.
sample: Could I ask what you meant by “write more academically” on my assignment? I’m not sure whether I should work on my vocabulary, sentence structure or something else. Could you show me a sentence that needs improvement and explain how you would revise it?

title: Noisy Friend
text: Your friend is sitting next to you and keeps talking, but you want to focus on the lecture and take notes. What would you say to him?
facts: A friend is talking during a lecture and interrupting note-taking.
Ask the friend quietly to pause the conversation until after class.
sample: Hey, could we talk after the lecture? I’m having trouble following what the lecturer is saying and I need to take some notes. I’d like to hear the rest of what you were saying when we’re finished.

title: Wrong Email
text: Your professor says he hasn't received your assignment by email. You check your email and find that you have sent it to the wrong address. What would you say to your professor?
facts: The professor did not receive the assignment because it went to the wrong email address.
Acknowledge the mistake and offer to resend the assignment promptly.
sample: Professor, I checked my sent messages and found that I sent the assignment to the wrong address. I’m sorry for the mistake. I’ll resend it to your correct address now, and I can forward the original message if you need to check when I first sent it.

title: Food Preference
text: Your friend wants to go to Anne's Caff, which serves pizza and sandwiches, but you would like to try a different place with other dishes. How would you respond to your friend?
facts: A friend suggests Anne’s Caff for pizza and sandwiches, but the speaker wants other dishes.
Express the preference tactfully and suggest a different place to try together.
sample: Anne’s Caff is an option, but I’m in the mood for something other than pizza or sandwiches today. Would you be up for trying a different place with a wider menu? We could look at a couple of places nearby and pick one we both like.

title: Library Etiquette
text: You are studying in a library and notice that some students nearby are talking loudly. How would you approach them and politely let them know that they are disturbing others?
facts: Students are talking loudly near others studying in a library.
Explain the disruption politely and ask the group to lower their voices.
sample: Excuse me, would you mind speaking a little more quietly? I’m trying to study and the conversation is carrying across this area. If you need to keep talking as a group, there might be a discussion space where you can speak more freely. Thanks for understanding.

title: Forgotten Keys
text: You forgot to bring the keys to your dorm and the door is locked so you can't get in. You need to call the school management team and ask them to solve this problem. What should you say?
facts: The resident forgot the dorm keys and is locked out.
Call school management, give the necessary location or identity details and ask for help gaining access.
sample: Hello, I’m a student living in the dorm and I’ve accidentally left my keys behind. My room is locked and I can’t get in. Could someone help me open it or tell me where to get a spare key? I can give you my room number and show you my student ID.

title: Difficult Course
text: You have taken a course for one semester. Now your friend tells you they also want to take this course and asks for your advice. Since the course is too difficult, you do not recommend it. What should you say?
facts: A friend asks whether to take a course the speaker found too difficult.
Explain why the speaker would discourage taking it and suggest checking alternatives.
sample: I took that course last semester and found the material very demanding. I’d hesitate to recommend it unless you already feel comfortable with the basics and have plenty of time for the work. Why don’t we compare the syllabus with a few other courses you’re considering?

title: Feedback of Assignment
text: You wrote an assignment, consulted your tutor, and asked them for some feedback on your work. What would you say to him?
facts: The speaker wants feedback from a tutor on a completed assignment.
Ask the tutor for focused comments on strengths and areas to improve.
sample: Could you give me some feedback on the assignment I wrote? I’d like to know whether my main argument comes across clearly and whether the structure supports it. If there’s one part you think I should work on first, could you point it out?

title: Subject Change
text: After choosing Subject A, you're thinking about changing it and consult your tutor about Subject B. What would you say?
facts: The student is considering switching from Subject A to Subject B.
Ask the tutor for guidance on fit, requirements and the process for switching.
sample: I’ve enrolled in Subject A, but I’m thinking about switching to Subject B. Do you think it would be a good fit for my study plans? Could you tell me whether there are any prerequisites or deadlines I should know about before I decide?

title: Broken Printer
text: You want to copy some documents, but you notice the printer is broken and the red light is flashing. What would you say to the administrator?
facts: A printer needed to copy documents is broken with a flashing red light.
Report the fault to the administrator and ask for assistance or another machine.
sample: Excuse me, I’m trying to copy some documents, but this printer isn’t working and the red light is flashing. Could you take a look, please? If it can’t be fixed now, could you point me to another machine I can use?

title: Online Class Absence
text: Your computer is broken and you can't attend the online class. How should you tell your professor?
facts: A broken computer prevents the student from attending an online class.
Tell the professor promptly and ask how to catch up or join by another route.
sample: Professor, my computer has broken down and I can’t join today’s online class. I wanted to let you know before it begins. Is there a recording or a set of notes I could use to catch up? If there’s another way to join from my phone, I’m happy to try it.

title: Cafe Advertisement
text: You see a job advertisement for a caff, but you're not sure if it's still valid, so you go and ask the manager and inquire about the tasks of the position being advertised. What would you say?
facts: The speaker saw a café job advertisement and wants to know whether it is current.
Ask the manager if applications are still open and what the job involves.
sample: Hello, I saw an advertisement for a position at your café and wanted to ask whether it’s still open. If you’re still taking applications, could you tell me what duties the job involves and how I should apply?

title: Noisy Flatmates
text: Your flatmates are holding a party in their room at night, which is too noisy for you to sleep, but you have an important exam early tomorrow morning. What should you say to them?
facts: Flatmates are holding a noisy party at night before the speaker’s early exam.
Explain the immediate concern without blaming them and ask for a quieter arrangement.
sample: Hey, could you turn the music down a bit? I have an important exam early tomorrow and I can’t get to sleep with the noise coming from your room. I know you’re enjoying the party, but could you keep the volume down or move somewhere you won’t disturb people trying to sleep?

title: Deadline Request
text: The deadline for your assignment is approaching, but your computer is broken, and you want to ask your teacher for an extension. What would you say?
facts: An approaching assignment deadline and a broken computer put submission at risk.
Explain the problem to the teacher and request a realistic extension.
sample: My assignment is due soon, but my computer has broken down and I’m having trouble finishing the work in time. Could I have a short extension while I arrange access to another computer? Please let me know whether I should submit a formal request.

title: Assignment Extension Request
text: You are in your second year of university and have been working on a big assignment for your psychology class. Unfortunately, you've had the flu for the past week and couldn't concentrate or get much work done. You have a doctor's note and feel a little better now. You go to your lecturer's office to talk. What would you say?
facts: A second-year psychology student lost work time to the flu and has a doctor’s note.
Explain the situation to the lecturer, offer documentation and ask for more time.
sample: I’m here about the psychology assignment. I’ve had the flu for the past week and I couldn’t concentrate enough to make much progress. I’m starting to feel better and I have a doctor’s note. Could I please have a few extra days to finish the work?

title: Lecture Assistance
text: You are walking out of a lecture and realize that you didn't fully understand some of the main points your professor discussed. You notice a classmate who seemed to take good notes and was paying close attention during class. You want to ask them for help in understanding what was covered. What would you say?
facts: The speaker missed some main points in a lecture and a classmate took good notes.
Ask the classmate to explain unclear points or briefly share their notes.
sample: Hey, did you have a minute to go over the lecture? I didn’t quite follow some of the professor’s main points and I noticed you took detailed notes. Would you mind talking me through what I missed, or showing me that section of your notes?

title: Writing Guidance
text: You are working on an essay for your course and you are having difficulty organizing your ideas. You approach your professor after class and ask her if you could come to her office to discuss your essay. What do you say to her?
facts: The student is having difficulty organising ideas in an essay.
Ask the professor after class for an office meeting to discuss the draft or outline.
sample: Professor, could I come by during your office hours to ask about my essay? I have some ideas, but I’m struggling to organise them into a clear argument. I can bring my outline and show you where I’m getting stuck. When would be a good time?

title: Chip Discount
text: You purchased chips at a supermarket where there was a discount offer of 2 for 3 dollars. However, at the checkout, you noticed that you were charged 3 dollars for each bag instead. How would you politely point out the pricing error to the cashier and ask for a correction?
facts: A promotion offered two bags of chips for three dollars, but each bag was charged three dollars.
Politely point out the discrepancy and ask the cashier to correct the charge.
sample: Excuse me, could you check the price of these chips? The sign said two bags for three dollars, but it looks like I was charged three dollars for each bag. Would you mind checking the offer and correcting the total if it applies?

title: Restaurant Order
text: You're dining at a restaurant and ordered a hamburger, but the waiter brings you fish and chips by mistake. How would you politely point out the error and ask for the correct order?
facts: A waiter brought fish and chips when the customer ordered a hamburger.
Politely explain the mix-up and ask for the ordered meal.
sample: Excuse me, I think there’s been a mix-up. I ordered the hamburger, but I’ve been served fish and chips. Would you mind checking the order and bringing me the hamburger, please? Thanks for sorting it out.

title: Cat
text: You're going to be away from home for three days and need someone to look after your cat. You'd like to ask your friend Monica if she can help by feeding your cat during that time. How would you explain your situation to Monica and politely ask for her help?
facts: The speaker will be away for three days and needs Monica to feed the cat.
Ask Monica for help, offer practical feeding instructions and allow her to decline.
sample: Hi Monica, I’ll be out of town for three days. Would you be able to stop by and feed my cat while I’m away? I can leave a key and write down the feeding times and portions. If you’re busy, just let me know so I can make another arrangement.

title: Wind
text: Your classmate is currently away on vacation, and you're at her home. Due to strong winds, some of the balcony furniture has been damaged. You want to let her know about the situation so she can be mentally prepared before returning. What would you say to her in a thoughtful and considerate way?
facts: Strong winds damaged some balcony furniture at a classmate’s home while she was away.
Let her know gently before she returns and offer to send details or photos.
sample: Hi, I wanted to let you know before you get home that the strong winds damaged some of your balcony furniture. I know that’s upsetting news to get while you’re away. I can send you photos and explain what I saw whenever you have a moment.

title: Call and Dinner
text: You're in the middle of preparing dinner when your friend calls to talk about a problem her daughter is facing. You genuinely want to help, but you're currently busy. You'd like to ask if she could call you a bit later. What would you say to your friend to express your concern and request a better time to talk?
facts: A friend calls about her daughter while the speaker is preparing dinner.
Express concern and ask the friend to call back when the speaker can listen well.
sample: I’m sorry to hear your daughter is having a difficult time, and I’d like to hear what’s going on. I’m in the middle of making dinner right now. Could you call me a little later, when I can give you my full attention?

title: Borrowed Book
text: You borrowed a book from your friend Anit, and she has asked for it back. You want to politely arrange its return and find a time that works for her to pick it up. What would you say to Anit to make the return easy and convenient for both of you?
facts: Anit has asked for a borrowed book back.
Thank her for lending it and arrange a convenient time for her to collect it.
sample: Thanks for lending me the book, Anit. I have it ready for you to pick up. Would this evening work for you? If you’d prefer another time, tell me what’s convenient and I’ll make sure I’m there to give it to you.

title: Garden Care
text: You're getting ready to leave for a vacation and are concerned about your garden plants. One morning, you notice your neighbor at her door. You'd like to ask if she could kindly water your plants twice a week while you're away. What would you say to her?
facts: The speaker will be on vacation and wants a neighbor to water their plants twice a week.
Ask politely and offer clear instructions and access arrangements.
sample: Hi, I’m getting ready to go away on vacation. Would you mind watering my garden plants twice a week while I’m gone? I can show you which plants need watering and where I keep the hose. Please say if the timing won’t work for you.

title: Wet Floor
text: As you were walking up the stairs to your apartment, you nearly slipped because the floor was wet. You decide to inform one of your neighbors to make them aware and possibly prevent any accidents. What do you say to your neighbor?
facts: Wet stairs at the apartment nearly caused the speaker to slip.
Warn the neighbor of the location and suggest a practical way to prevent an accident.
sample: Just a heads-up: the floor on the stairs is wet and I nearly slipped coming up. Please be careful if you go that way. I’ll let building management know so they can put up a warning sign and get it cleaned up.

title: Wrong Delivery
text: You've received a letter at your home that's actually meant for your neighbor. What would you say when you go to return the letter and explain the mistake politely?
facts: A neighbor’s letter was delivered to the speaker’s home.
Return the letter and explain the delivery mix-up politely.
sample: Hi, this letter was delivered to my house by mistake. I saw your name on the envelope, so I thought I’d bring it over. Here you go. I wanted to make sure it reached you.

title: Flight Canceled
text: Your flight has been canceled, so instead of going to the airport, you now need to go home. You had already told the taxi driver to head to the airport. What would you say to the driver to explain the change and give directions to your home?
facts: A flight cancellation changes a taxi trip from the airport to the speaker’s home.
Tell the driver promptly and give the new destination or directions.
sample: Excuse me, I’ve just found out my flight has been cancelled. Could you take me home instead of to the airport? I’ll give you my address and show you the location on the map. Please let me know if you need me to update the trip in the app.

title: Late to School
text: You are late to school today and need to explain the situation to your teacher. How would you apologize for being late and provide a reasonable explanation for your delay?
facts: The student has arrived late to school.
Apologise to the teacher, give a reasonable explanation and acknowledge missed work.
sample: I’m sorry I’m late. My usual bus didn’t arrive this morning, so I had to wait for the next one. I’ll take a seat quietly, and after class I’ll check what I missed so I can catch up.

title: Italian Food
text: You are going to eat outside with your friends and they want to eat Italian food. You don't like Italian food, but you want to dine out with them. What would you say to your friends?
facts: Friends want Italian food, which the speaker dislikes, but the speaker wants to join them.
Be tactful about the preference and suggest an option that works for everyone.
sample: I’d love to have dinner with you. Italian food isn’t usually my first choice, though. Would you consider somewhere that offers a mix of dishes? If you really want Italian, let’s check the menu together and see if there’s something I’d enjoy too.

title: Lazy Roommate
text: You have a roommate, but he usually does not clean the common areas. You cannot stand dirty common areas. You're going to talk to him. What are you going to say?
facts: A roommate regularly leaves shared areas dirty.
Describe the concern calmly and suggest a fair cleaning arrangement.
sample: Could we talk about keeping the common areas clean? Lately I’ve been finding the kitchen and living area messy after they’ve been used, and it makes sharing the space frustrating. Could we each clean up after ourselves and agree on a simple schedule for the bigger jobs?

title: Project Extension
text: You are enrolled in evening business classes, and your project deadline is approaching. You feel you need more time and would like to request an extension through the weekend. You decide to visit your professor during office hours. How would you politely ask for an extension?
facts: An evening business class project is due soon and the student needs through the weekend.
Make a specific extension request to the professor during office hours.
sample: Professor, could I ask about the deadline for our business project? I’ve made progress, but I need some more time to finish the work properly. Would it be possible for me to submit it after the weekend? I can show you what I’ve completed so far if that helps.

title: Dessert
text: One of your friends, whom you've invited to your party, offers to bring dessert. However, you've already made dessert and would prefer if they brought something else, like fruit or snacks. How would you politely respond to your friend's offer?
facts: A party guest has offered dessert, but dessert is already made.
Thank them and suggest fruit or snacks as an alternative.
sample: Thanks for offering to bring dessert! I’ve actually made one already. If you’d still like to bring something, some fruit or savoury snacks would be lovely. Please don’t feel you have to bring anything, though. I’m just glad you can come.

title: Countryside Walk
text: How would you respond to your friend Susan's suggestion to go for a countryside walk tomorrow, letting her know you'd love to join but prefer to wait until the morning to decide, since the weather forecast predicts rain?
facts: Susan proposes a countryside walk tomorrow, with rain in the forecast.
Show interest and suggest deciding in the morning after checking the weather.
sample: I’d love to go for a walk with you, Susan. The forecast says it might rain tomorrow, so could we check the weather in the morning before we decide? If it looks clear, we can still go. If not, we could choose another day.

title: Farewell Gift
text: How would you start a conversation with your colleagues to discuss ideas for a farewell gift for your manager, Joe, who is retiring and planning to travel abroad?
facts: Manager Joe is retiring and plans to travel abroad.
Invite colleagues to suggest a farewell gift that relates to Joe’s travel plans.
sample: Has anyone thought about a farewell gift for Joe? Since he’s retiring and planning to travel abroad, we could get him something useful for the trip, perhaps a travel voucher or a lightweight travel bag. Does anyone know his plans well enough to suggest something he’d really enjoy?

title: Waiter's Complaint
text: How would you politely give feedback to the restaurant manager, mentioning that you enjoyed the food but were disappointed with the waiter's service and the missing coffee order?
facts: The meal was enjoyable, but the waiter’s service was disappointing and coffee never arrived.
Give the manager balanced, specific feedback and ask about the missing order if needed.
sample: Could I share some feedback about our visit? We really enjoyed the food, but the service was disappointing. We ordered coffee and it never arrived, even though we waited for it. I’d appreciate it if you could check whether the coffee was added to our bill.

title: Sam's Cafe
text: During your dinner date, how would you politely tell your friend that you'd prefer to eat at a restaurant with a full menu rather than going to Sam's Cafe, which mainly offers drinks?
facts: Sam’s Cafe mainly offers drinks, and the speaker wants a full meal on a dinner date.
Respectfully suggest dining at a full-menu restaurant.
sample: Sam’s Cafe sounds good for drinks, but I was hoping we could sit down for a proper dinner. Would you be open to a place with a full menu instead? We could always stop by Sam’s for a drink afterwards if you’d like.

title: Competition Conflict
text: You have a tutorial scheduled for 3 P .M. on Monday, but you've been selected to participate in an important competition at the same time. You need to inform your teacher and request a solution. What would you say?
facts: A Monday 3 p.m. tutorial clashes with an important competition.
Tell the teacher about the conflict and ask about another tutorial or catching up.
sample: I’ve been selected to take part in an important competition at three on Monday, which clashes with my tutorial. Could I attend another session that week? If that isn’t possible, could you tell me what I should do to catch up on the material?

title: Extension Request
text: You've been given a deadline for an assignment, but due to a personal emergency, you need more time to finish it. How would you approach your professor to request an extension and ensure the situation is handled appropriately? What would you say?
facts: A personal emergency affects an assignment deadline.
Disclose only necessary details and ask the professor for an extension and the correct process.
sample: Professor, I’ve had a personal emergency and won’t be able to finish the assignment by the deadline. Could I please have a short extension? I’m happy to suggest a new date and follow the formal request process if that’s required.

title: Slippery Stairs Safety
text: You notice that the stairs at your workplace are wet and slippery, which could pose a safety hazard. What would you say to your colleagues or supervisor to address the situation and ensure the area is made safe for everyone?
facts: Wet and slippery workplace stairs pose a safety hazard.
Warn people promptly and ask for the area to be marked off and cleaned.
sample: Please be careful on these stairs. They’re wet and very slippery. Could we put up a warning sign and ask the cleaning team to dry them? Until the area is safe, we should let people know to use another route if one is available.

title: Declining Dinner Invitation
text: A colleague has invited you to dinner, but you are unable to attend due to prior commitments. How would you politely turn down the invitation while expressing your appreciation? What key points would you mention to maintain a positive relationship?
facts: A colleague’s dinner invitation conflicts with a prior commitment.
Thank the colleague, decline politely and signal interest in meeting another time.
sample: Thanks so much for inviting me to dinner. I already have something arranged that evening, so I won’t be able to make it. I really appreciate you thinking of me. I’d love to join you another time if we can find a date that suits us both.

title: Dinner Invitation Preferences
text: You've invited a friend to dinner at your place. However, you're unsure about their food preferences or dietary restrictions. You decide to call them, but they don't answer. How would you leave a message asking about their food preferences to ensure you prepare something they would enjoy?
facts: An invited dinner guest did not answer the phone, and their food preferences are unknown.
Leave a friendly voicemail asking about preferences and dietary restrictions.
sample: Hi, it’s me. I’m planning dinner for when you come over and wanted to check if there’s anything you don’t eat or any allergies I should know about. Is there a dish you especially like? Give me a call or send me a message when you get a chance.

title: Suggesting Train Route
text: Your friend is planning to visit a location far from their home and is considering driving. However, you believe taking the train could be a more convenient option. Your friend is undecided between driving and taking the train. How would you recommend the train as the better choice, and what key points would you emphasize to convince them of its advantages?
facts: A friend considering a long drive is open to taking the train.
Recommend checking the train as an alternative and explain practical advantages without overpromising.
sample: Have you looked into taking the train? For a trip that far, it could save you the effort of driving for hours and finding parking. You’d be able to relax on the way. I’d compare the ticket price, travel time and how far the station is from your destination before deciding.

title: Gift for Manager
text: Your manager is retiring soon, and you want to buy a thoughtful gift. How would you approach a friend or colleague for advice on selecting and purchasing the gift, including choosing something that reflects their interests, setting a budget, coordinating with others for a group gift, and ensuring a meaningful presentation?
facts: A colleague or friend can help plan a manager’s retirement gift.
Ask for ideas based on interests, agree on a budget, organise optional contributions and plan the presentation.
sample: Could you help me choose a retirement gift for our manager? Do you know what they enjoy outside work? We could agree on a budget, ask the team if they’d like to contribute and choose something that reflects their interests. A signed card and a short presentation at the farewell would make it more personal.

title: Dining Out
text: You and your friends have different restaurant preferences for a night out. How should you approach the conversation to express your preference for a different restaurant, and what points should you cover to reach a compromise that considers everyone's opinions?
facts: Friends want different restaurants for a night out.
Express a preference, ask what matters to the others and suggest a compromise.
sample: I’d prefer to try a different restaurant tonight, but I’d like us to pick somewhere everyone can enjoy. What matters most to each of you: the food, the price or the location? We could compare a couple of menus and choose a place with dishes that suit everyone.

title: Late for Meeting
text: You are late by 10 minutes for a meeting due to a broken car and heavy traffic. How do you approach your colleagues or boss to explain your delay? What key points should you mention?
facts: A car breakdown and heavy traffic made the speaker ten minutes late for a meeting.
Apologise, explain briefly and offer to catch up without disrupting the meeting.
sample: I’m sorry I’m ten minutes late. My car broke down, and heavy traffic delayed me further after I arranged another way here. Please carry on. I’ll check the notes for anything I missed and catch up afterwards if I have questions.

title: Relative's Appointment
text: You have an appointment and need to leave work early to accompany a relative. How do you request permission from your employer for early departure? What key points should you address to ensure your request is understood and approved?
facts: The speaker must accompany a relative to an appointment and needs to leave work early.
Ask the employer for permission, give the departure time and arrange coverage.
sample: Could I leave early today to accompany a relative to an appointment? I’d need to leave at about three. I can finish my priority tasks before I go and check with the team that anything urgent is covered. Would that arrangement work for you?

title: Family Member
text: You need to leave work early to drive a family member to see the doctor. How do you approach your boss to explain the situation? What specific points do you include to ensure understanding and approval of your request?
facts: The speaker must drive a family member to see a doctor and needs to leave work early.
Explain the reason to the boss, ask permission and address the work handover.
sample: Could I leave work a little early today to drive a family member to a doctor’s appointment? I need to leave by three to get there on time. I’ll finish what I can beforehand and hand over any urgent work. Please let me know if there’s anything you’d like me to prioritise before I go.

title: Car Breakdown
text: Your car has broken down, and you know a girl is waiting for you. How do you approach this situation to inform her of the delay and ask for assistance or suggest alternative arrangements? What specific details do you include to ensure clear communication and to propose a solution that accommodates both of your needs?
facts: The speaker’s car broke down while someone was waiting to meet them.
Notify her promptly, give an update and offer a practical alternative.
sample: Hi, I’m sorry to keep you waiting. My car has broken down and I’m arranging help, so I can’t get there on time. Would you prefer to meet a little later, or should we make another plan? I’ll update you as soon as I know when I can leave.

title: Borrowing an Umbrella
text: You've just arrived at the office and realized that it's pouring rain outside. You didn't bring an umbrella and know that one of your colleagues, who sits near you, often has a spare. How do you approach your colleague to ask for an umbrella, and what specific points do you include to ensure a positive response?
facts: It is pouring rain and a nearby colleague may have a spare umbrella.
Ask courteously to borrow it and say when it will be returned.
sample: Hi, I forgot my umbrella and it’s pouring outside. Do you happen to have your spare with you today? If you don’t need it, could I borrow it when I leave? I’ll bring it back tomorrow. No worries if you need it yourself.

title: Carpool
text: You have noticed that one of your colleagues lives in the same building as you and you are planning to approach them to travel together to work to avoid parking fees. Try to cover the following details: - Welcoming the idea of carpooling - Benefits of traveling together - Logistics such as meeting time and location - Any other relevant information to coordinate the carpool
facts: A colleague in the same building might share the commute to avoid parking fees.
Invite them to carpool, explain the benefits and propose a meeting time, location and sharing arrangement.
sample: Since we live in the same building, would you be interested in carpooling to work? We could cut down on parking costs and take turns driving. Could we try meeting outside the main entrance at eight on Monday? We can work out a schedule and how to split fuel and parking if it suits us both.

title: Movie Invitation
text: You are sick so you can't attend the invitation for the movie. Your friend in the lunchroom is having coffee, inform him about the situation.
facts: The speaker is sick and cannot go to a movie with a friend in the lunchroom.
Tell the friend directly, thank them for inviting you and suggest rescheduling if appropriate.
sample: Hey, thanks for inviting me to the movie. I’m feeling unwell today, so I’m going to head home and won’t be able to come. Please go ahead if you still want to see it. I’d love to catch a movie together once I’m feeling better.

title: Bike Rental Inquiry
text: You overheard your colleagues discussing about renting bikes, which sounds really fun and you are interested in it. Speak to your colleagues and inquire about the details, such as the cost of renting and how and where you can rent a bike.
facts: The speaker overheard colleagues talking about bike rentals and wants to try it.
Ask colleagues where and how to rent a bike and what it costs.
sample: I heard you talking about renting bikes, and it sounds like fun. Where do you usually rent them, and how much does it cost? Do I need to book online or can I turn up on the day? I’d appreciate any tips for getting started.

title: Lost Cafe Bag
text: Yesterday, you went to a cafe and forgot your bag, which contained your college materials. You were sitting by the window at lunchtime. Now, you need to call the cafe and discuss your forgotten bag. How would you respond to that?
facts: A bag containing college materials was left at a café, near the window at lunchtime yesterday.
Call the café, explain where and when the bag was left, and ask about collection.
sample: Hello, I think I left my bag at your café yesterday. I was sitting by the window at lunchtime, and the bag has my college materials in it. Has anyone handed it in? I can describe it in more detail and come by to collect it if you have it.

title: Restaurant Feedback
text: You and your friends went to a local restaurant where you encountered several issues with the quality and service. The long wait times, small meal portions, and the coffee you ordered never arrived. Now, the manager is asking for your feedback after the meal. How would you respond to that?
facts: At a restaurant, a group experienced a long wait, small portions and missing coffee.
Tell the manager about all three concerns in constructive terms.
sample: Thanks for asking. We waited a long time for the meals, and the portions were smaller than we expected. We also ordered coffee, but it never arrived. Could you check what happened with that order? I wanted to let you know because these issues affected our visit.

title: Busy with dinner
text: A friend called you to discuss a problem with one of her children. Let her know that you are busy preparing dinner and that you will call her later to help with the issue. How do you handle such situations?
facts: A friend calls about one of her children while the speaker is preparing dinner.
Show concern, explain the timing and promise to call her back to help.
sample: I’m sorry to hear your child is having trouble. I’d like to talk it through with you, but I’m in the middle of cooking dinner right now. I’ll call you as soon as I’ve finished so I can give you my full attention and see how I can help.

title: Late Return Apology
text: You borrowed a book from the library and forgot to return it on time. Now, there's a late fee, and you need to explain the delay to the librarian and possibly request a waiver or reduction of the fee. What is your conversation like?
facts: A borrowed library book was returned late because the speaker forgot, and a fee is due.
Apologise, accept responsibility and politely ask about a fee waiver or reduction.
sample: I’m sorry I returned this book late. I forgot the due date and I realise that was my responsibility. Is there any chance the late fee could be waived or reduced? If that isn’t possible, could you tell me how to pay it?

title: A Spa Day
text: You book a spa day based on glowing reviews and a wide range of services listed online. When you arrive, half the services are unavailable, and the facilities are not as advertised. How do you address this with the spa manager?
facts: A spa advertised numerous services and facilities, but many are unavailable or different on arrival.
Explain the gap to the spa manager and ask for a fair resolution.
sample: I booked today based on the treatments and facilities listed on your website. I’ve arrived to find that several of those services are unavailable and the facilities are different from what was advertised. Could you tell me what is available and whether a partial refund or a new booking is possible?

title: Mess Bike
text: You've lent your bicycle to a friend for a few days, but when they return it, you notice it's covered in mud, the tires are deflated, and there are scratches on the frame. You're disappointed with the lack of care and want to remind your friend. What would you say to your friend?
facts: A borrowed bicycle came back muddy, with deflated tyres and scratches.
Explain the concern to the friend, ask what happened and propose a remedy.
sample: Could we talk about the bike? When you brought it back, it was covered in mud, the tyres were flat and there were scratches on the frame. I was disappointed to see it come back like that. Do you know what happened? Could you help clean it and check whether it needs any repairs?

title: Noise Control
text: You've organized a group study session with your classmates at your apartment. However, when they arrive, you notice some of them are not following the agreed-upon noise level and are causing disturbances to your neighbors. You need to remind them to be considerate of others. What would you say to your classmates?
facts: A study group at the speaker’s apartment is louder than agreed and is disturbing neighbors.
Remind classmates of the agreement and ask them to lower their voices.
sample: Could we keep our voices down a bit? We agreed to keep the study session quiet, and the sound is carrying to my neighbours. Let’s talk one at a time and keep side conversations low. If we need a louder group discussion, we can arrange to meet somewhere else next time.

title: Flawed Project
text: You're a project manager who has just reviewed a team's project draft due next week. You notice several critical sections are incomplete, and the overall quality is below expectations. You need to address these issues promptly while motivating the team to improve their work before the deadline. What would you say to your team?
facts: A project draft due next week has critical gaps and falls below expectations.
Motivate the team while assigning corrective priorities and a review before the deadline.
sample: Thanks for getting a draft together. I’ve reviewed it and several important sections are still incomplete. We need to bring the whole draft up to standard before next week’s deadline. Let’s agree who will finish each section, set an internal review date and flag any obstacles now so we can help each other.

title: Forgot Wallet
text: You're at a salon and you want to get a haircut, but you realize that you left your wallet in your taxi. You don't have the taxi number and you don't have any other payment methods with you. What will you tell the stylist in order to get this situation sorted?
facts: The customer left their wallet in a taxi, has no taxi number and cannot pay for a haircut.
Explain the problem before the service and ask to reschedule or resolve payment with the stylist.
sample: I’ve just realised I left my wallet in the taxi. I don’t have the taxi number and I don’t have another way to pay today. Could we reschedule the haircut while I try to locate my wallet? I’m sorry for the inconvenience.

title: Request Professor
text: You are supposed to submit an essay by tomorrow, but you have been unwell for a fortnight. You have a medical certificate from the clinic. You have recovered now, but you need more time to finish your essay. You visit your professor's office. How do you request him for an extension over the weekend?
facts: An essay is due tomorrow after a fortnight of illness, and the student has a medical certificate.
Explain the situation to the professor, offer the certificate and ask for a weekend extension.
sample: Professor, my essay is due tomorrow, but I’ve been unwell for the past two weeks and fell behind. I’ve recovered and have a medical certificate from the clinic. Could I have the weekend to finish the essay and submit it on Monday? I can show you the certificate.

title: Presentation
text: You have a presentation at 9 am and your laptop crashed. Call your professor and ask for an extension or an alternative way to submit your work.
facts: A laptop crash puts a 9 a.m. presentation at risk.
Call the professor immediately and ask for a delay or alternative way to submit.
sample: Professor, I’m calling about my nine o’clock presentation. My laptop has crashed and I’m worried I won’t be able to access my slides in time. Could I present later today, or would you accept the material another way if I can retrieve it?

title: Doctor's Appointment
text: You had a doctor's appointment at 10 am and you were late. Explain at the reception the reason for your delay and request the reception to know if you can see the doctor later today.
facts: The patient missed a 10 a.m. appointment by arriving late.
Explain a reasonable cause at reception, apologise and ask about being seen later today.
sample: Hello, I had an appointment at ten this morning. I’m sorry I arrived late. My bus was delayed and I couldn’t get here in time. Is there any chance the doctor could see me later today, perhaps if there’s a cancellation?

title: Group Project
text: You're working on a group project with three other classmates and you have a deadline coming up soon. One of your group members has not contributed anything so far and is not responding to your messages. What would you say to your group member and your other teammates?
facts: A group member has made no contribution or replied, and the project deadline is near.
Check in with the missing member directly and talk to the other teammates about a fallback plan.
sample: To our missing teammate, I’d say: We haven’t heard from you and the project is due soon. Is everything okay? Could you let us know today whether you can finish your section or need help? To the others, I’d say: Let’s agree on how to cover that work if we don’t hear back today, so we can still submit on time.
